item.text: {"search_note":"I did not find a clean 2024 source proving a direct Khamenei family-business transaction, named relative benefiting from a contract, or a single smoking-gun case of personal enrichment tied to one state decision. The evidence is mostly structural and indirect, but it is consistent across elections, oil exports, economic control, and oversight bodies.","evidence":[{"title":"Iran’s Revolutionary Guards extend control over Tehran’s oil exports, sources say","publisher":"Reuters via Investing.com","date":"2024-12-18","url":"https://www.investing.com/news/commodities-news/irans-revolutionary-guards-extend-control-over-tehrans-oil-exports-sources-say-3778558","summary":"Strong negative evidence: Reuters reported the IRGC controlled up to half of Iran’s oil exports, using shadow fleets and front companies. Since oil revenue funds state spending, this points to capture by regime-security networks rather than separation from public-resource decisions.","question_ids":["7B.3","6B.10","7B.1"]},{"title":"Iran's presidential election dominated by Khamenei loyalists","publisher":"Reuters via Investing.com","date":"2024-06-25","url":"https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/irans-presidential-election-dominated-by-khamenei-loyalists-3494879","summary":"Strong negative evidence: Reuters said Khamenei ensured hardline candidates dominated the contest, the Guardian Council approved only five hardliners and one low-profile moderate from 80 applicants, and his adviser wanted a president whose views did not conflict with the supreme leader. This is loyalty filtering, not an arm’s-length state.","question_ids":["7B.3","7B.1","7B.2"]},{"title":"Pezeshkian Cabinet: Profiles","publisher":"The Iran Primer / USIP","date":"2024-08-22","url":"https://iranprimer.usip.org/index.php/blog/2024/aug/22/pezeshkian-cabinet-profiles","summary":"Weak positive evidence: the cabinet included reformists, hardliners, technocrats, and academics, and the list reportedly had Khamenei, IRGC, and security-agency approval before submission. That suggests limited technocratic inclusion, but it is compromise-driven and still inside a Khamenei-approved political envelope.","question_ids":["7B.3","6B.10"]},{"title":"Who are the key ministers in Iran's new government?","publisher":"The National","date":"2024-08-22","url":"https://www.thenationalnews.com/news/mena/2024/08/22/who-are-the-key-ministers-in-irans-new-government/","summary":"Weak positive evidence: the cabinet mixed technocrats with security-linked and ideological figures, while the interior and intelligence portfolios stayed in the security orbit. This points to some professionalization, but not a real wall between state administration and regime networks.","question_ids":["7B.3"]},{"title":"Iran holds presidential vote with limited choices","publisher":"Reuters via Investing.com","date":"2024-06-27","url":"https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/iran-holds-presidential-vote-with-limited-choices-3500514","summary":"Strong negative background evidence: Reuters said the race was tightly controlled and candidates talked about reviving the economy without concrete plans. That supports a picture of a managed patronage system, not neutral institutions separating public decisions from loyalist advantage.","question_ids":["7B.3","7B.1","7B.2"]},{"title":"Iran: Freedom in the World 2024 Country Report","publisher":"Freedom House","date":"2024","url":"https://freedomhouse.org/country/iran/freedom-world/2024","summary":"Strong negative background: Freedom House says corruption is endemic, IRGC and bonyads are above scrutiny, and powerful institutions dominate the economy. This is broad evidence that regime-linked interests remain embedded in state and economic decisions.","question_ids":["7B.3","6B.10","7B.1"]},{"title":"Factbox: Key facts about Iran's elections on Friday","publisher":"Reuters via ThePrint","date":"2024-02-29","url":"https://theprint.in/world/factbox-key-facts-about-irans-elections-on-friday/1983652/","summary":"Strong negative structural evidence: Reuters explains that Assembly of Experts candidates must pass Guardian Council vetting and that the body is supposed to choose or dismiss the supreme leader. In practice, that institution is tightly controlled, not independent from Khamenei’s camp.","question_ids":["7B.3","6B.9"]},{"title":"Iran bans ex-president Rouhani from running for elite assembly","publisher":"Reuters via ThePrint","date":"2024-01-24","url":"https://theprint.in/world/iran-bans-ex-president-rouhani-from-running-for-elite-assembly/1937211/","summary":"Strong negative evidence: disqualifying Rouhani from the Assembly of Experts shows even nominal oversight bodies were kept under loyalty control. That is hard to reconcile with any clean separation of personal power from state institutions.","question_ids":["7B.3","6B.9","7B.1"]}]}
